facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains
A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

concepts.why: The patient has a history of T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia and is receiving maintenance therapy, which increases the risk of graft-versus-host disease, and the presence of mixed inflammatory infiltrate and basophilic inclusions in the histiocytes supports this diagnosis.

The patient is receiving maintenance therapy with 6-mercaptopurine, methotrexate, vincristine, and dexamethasone, which can cause colitis, and the presence of hematochezia, loose bowel movements, and erythematous mucosa supports this diagnosis.
The patient has a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid, which is a possible cause of the hematochezia.
The patient has a history of hematochezia, loose bowel movements, and mixed inflammatory infiltrate, which are consistent with inflammatory bowel disease.

The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains, in the context of negative stool studies, suggests an alternative diagnosis.

rationales.F01: T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia may increase the risk of graft-versus-host disease.
rationales.F07: Neutropenia and lymphopenia can increase the risk of graft-versus-host disease.
rationales.F09: A nonbleeding external hemorrhoid is a common cause of hematochezia.
rationales.F11: The presence of polyps and erythematous mucosa is consistent with graft-versus-host disease and chemotherapy-induced colitis.
rationales.F12: The presence of basophilic inclusions in histiocytes is consistent with melanosis coli and graft-versus-host disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: Chemotherapy-induced colitis best explains the patient's symptoms of hematochezia and loose bowel movements, which are consistent with the side effects of chemotherapy, and the colonoscopy findings of multiple semisessile polyps with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa.
